source.version: Ca’ Foscari University of Venice, Department of Economics Working Paper No. 16/WP/2026 (PDF pp. 1-2). The bound Online Appendix is dated February 2026 (PDF p. 30); no distinct main-text revision date is printed.
source.supplement_used: Bound Online Appendix, PDF pp. 30-54 (appendix pp. 1-25): experimental instructions, construction of AI-involvement measures and code, and Appendix C mediation table. No separate local supplement was found.

studies.label: Laboratory experiment: AI access crossed with tournament, piece-rate, and lottery incentives
studies.cluster_se_treatment: Table 5 reports heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors for participant-level OLS; session clustering is not stated. Individual versus session treatment assignment and the number of randomized clusters are not established (PDF p. 8, printed p. 5; PDF p. 23, printed p. 20).

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 8 (printed p. 5), Section 2.1, Experimental Procedures; PDF p. 14 (printed p. 11), Table 1, Obs. row in column order T, PR, L, T&AI, PR&AI, L&AI
counts_source.quote: The experiment was conducted at VERALabEx (Ca’ Foscari University of Venice) with 360 participants, primarily students in economics-related programs. ... Obs. 52 47 49 88 62 62

arms.name: T
arms.description: Tournament incentive without AI access. The highest-rated composition in a randomly formed, gender-balanced group earns a payment per rating point; other group members receive no task payment (PDF p. 7, printed p. 4, Section 2.1).

arms.name: PR
arms.description: Piece-rate incentive without AI access. Payment is proportional to the mean external creativity rating (PDF p. 7, printed p. 4, Section 2.1).

arms.name: L
arms.description: Lottery incentive without AI access. One group member receives a fixed prize independently of performance (PDF p. 7, printed p. 4, Section 2.1).

arms.name: T&AI
arms.description: Tournament incentive with unrestricted ChatGPT access during composition; otherwise the same incentive rule as T (PDF p. 7, printed p. 4, Section 2.1).

arms.name: PR&AI
arms.description: Piece-rate incentive with unrestricted ChatGPT access during composition; otherwise the same incentive rule as PR (PDF p. 7, printed p. 4, Section 2.1).

arms.name: L&AI
arms.description: Lottery incentive with unrestricted ChatGPT access during composition; otherwise the same incentive rule as L (PDF p. 7, printed p. 4, Section 2.1).

studies.task: Write an Italian creative composition about what one would create through thought alone, followed by a post-experimental Divergent Association Test after ChatGPT access ended (PDF pp. 6-8, printed pp. 3-5; PDF p. 31, appendix p. 2).

ai_tool.name: ChatGPT-4.2
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 7 (printed p. 4), Section 2.1: ChatGPT-4.2 API embedded in the experimental interface; PDF p. 27 (printed p. 24), AI declaration. Model name transcribed as printed; its release year is not stated.

preregistration.where: No preregistration is identified in the main paper or bound appendices. The ethics approval on PDF p. 3 is not a preregistration.

studies.shared_sample: An unnamed separate paper examines Stage 2 competition choices from this laboratory experiment; its identifier and exact analyzed overlap are not supplied. PDF p. 8 (printed p. 5), Section 2.1: The impact of AI on competition choices (i.e. Stage 2) is examined in a separate study.

estimates.outcome: Average creativity score of the composition
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Mean of four independent, treatment-blind ratings of each participant’s single composition by Italian-speaking Prolific evaluators. Main text states a 1 to 10 scale; laboratory and rater instructions state 0 to 10. The PDF does not resolve the minimum (PDF p. 9, printed p. 6; PDF pp. 32 and 34, appendix pp. 3 and 5).

regression.model: OLS of Average score on AI access, Tournament and Piece Rate indicators, with an intercept and Lottery as the omitted incentive category. Full sample; no text length, DAT, query count, or other post-treatment controls. Table 5, column (1).

estimates.notes: Full-sample contrast of assignment to AI access, retaining participants who did not use it. The incentive indicators were assigned experimental factors. The paper prints no pooled AI or No-AI means or SDs; regression intercepts are not entered as arm means. The Table 5 omnibus F statistic and its p-value test the whole model and are not entered as the AI contrast. Counts for the AI and No-AI samples are explicitly printed in Table 2 and the full-sample outcome count in Table 5. se_basis describes the reported participant-level robust OLS analysis; whether session-level randomization requires different uncertainty remains unresolved. Section 2.2 names the average rating as the main outcome, but no preregistration is stated. Table 2 AI coefficients are excluded because they adjust for variables collected after treatment.

estimates.outcome: Divergent Association Test score after AI access ended
estimates.question: after_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Average semantic distance among the words supplied by one participant, on the stated 0 to 100 range; higher values indicate greater divergent thinking ability. The paper cites Olson et al. for DAT but does not name the embedding/scoring implementation. This is within-person associative variety, not diversity across different participants.

not_extracted.what: S1-O1: Table 2, column (1), AI-access coefficient (PDF p. 16, printed p. 13)
not_extracted.reason: The creativity regression adjusts for composition length and DAT measured after assignment. The extraction rule excludes effects adjusted for post-treatment variables; Table 5 supplies the eligible combined-arm specification.

not_extracted.what: S1-O1: Table 2, column (2), AI (use) and AI (no use) coefficients (PDF p. 16, printed p. 13)
not_extracted.reason: Actual query submission was self-selected after assignment. These are subgroup contrasts, and the model also controls for post-treatment composition length and DAT.

not_extracted.what: S1-O1: Table 2, column (3), AI-access and linear/quadratic query-intensity coefficients (PDF p. 16, printed p. 13)
not_extracted.reason: The AI coefficient conditions on realized query intensity, composition length, and post-experiment DAT. Query-intensity coefficients describe a nonrandom dose-response association, not contrasts between assigned AI configurations.

not_extracted.what: S1-O1: Table 2, columns (4)-(5), creativity associations estimated separately within No-AI and AI samples (PDF p. 16, printed p. 13)
not_extracted.reason: Within-arm covariate, ability, and query-intensity associations are subgroup analyses rather than full-sample randomized AI contrasts.

not_extracted.what: Main-text Table 3: SEM direct, indirect, and total effects on creativity and Similarity (PDF p. 18, printed p. 15)
not_extracted.reason: Mediation analyses restricted to participants with AI access, using self-selected ideation requests and downstream incorporation. No randomized AI-configuration contrast is estimated.

not_extracted.what: Appendix C, Table 1: SEM effects using AI-first and User-first keywords (PDF p. 53, appendix p. 24)
not_extracted.reason: Mediation analyses and observational indicators of AI reliance within the AI-access sample; excluded under the mediation and subgroup rules.

not_extracted.what: Similarity: Table 1, Table 4 column (3), and Table 5 column (6) (PDF pp. 14, 21, 23; printed pp. 11, 18, 20)
not_extracted.reason: TF-IDF cosine similarity compares each participant’s final composition with that participant’s own concatenated AI responses (PDF p. 36, appendix p. 7, Section B.4). It measures incorporation of AI text, not creativity or diversity across different people. No across_people outcome is reported.

not_extracted.what: AI (use): descriptive statistics and usage regressions in Tables 1, 4, and 5 (PDF pp. 14, 21, 23)
not_extracted.reason: Whether someone submitted a query is a process/adoption measure, not a creativity or diversity score on the produced output.

not_extracted.what: Number of queries filled: descriptive statistics and usage regressions in Tables 1, 4, and 5 (PDF pp. 14, 21, 23)
not_extracted.reason: Counts interactions with the chatbot, not creative ideas produced, and is not an eligible fluency or other output outcome.

not_extracted.what: Idea request: descriptive statistics and regressions in Tables 1, 4, and 5 (PDF pp. 14, 21, 23)
not_extracted.reason: Classifies whether the participant asked AI for an idea. This measures interaction strategy rather than the creativity of the produced output.

not_extracted.what: Idea request index: descriptive statistics and regressions in Tables 1, 4, and 5 (PDF pp. 14, 21, 23)
not_extracted.reason: The maximum query-classification ideation signal is a process measure, not a creativity or across-person-diversity outcome.

not_extracted.what: Books owned, AI exposure, and demographic characteristics in the questionnaire and Tables 1 and 4 (PDF pp. 8, 14, 21)
not_extracted.reason: Self-reported background/exposure and demographic covariates are not outcomes scored on participants’ creative outputs; their associations with AI use are not randomized contrasts.

not_extracted.what: Stage 2 competition choice (PDF p. 8, printed p. 5; PDF p. 33, appendix p. 4)
not_extracted.reason: Choice of payment scheme is outside the creativity-output scope. The paper states that this stage is analyzed in a separate, unnamed study and prints no eligible creative-output contrast for it.

not_extracted.what: Stage 3 beliefs about own score and rank (PDF p. 8, printed p. 5; PDF p. 33, appendix p. 4)
not_extracted.reason: Self-assessed expected performance is not an externally scored creative output; no eligible treatment contrast is reported.

not_extracted.what: Table 5 incentive coefficients, regression intercepts, and omnibus model statistics (PDF p. 23, printed p. 20)
not_extracted.reason: Tournament and Piece Rate coefficients compare incentive schemes, not AI availability or AI configurations. Intercepts are fitted baseline values, not observed arm means. Omnibus F statistics and their p-values do not test the single AI coefficient.

open_items: Assignment-stage total and per-arm randomized counts, exclusions/attrition, and reasons for unequal analyzed arm sizes are not printed. The printed participant and analysis counts do not establish the number originally assigned (PDF pp. 8, 14, 16, 23).

The paper states random assignment but does not specify individual versus session assignment. Session-treatment language and instructions do not establish the treatment-allocation protocol. Cluster counts and whether session-clustered uncertainty is needed remain unknown; the reported OLS SEs are robust, not explicitly clustered (PDF p. 8; PDF pp. 30-32; Table 5 on PDF p. 23).
The creativity-scale minimum conflicts: main text says 1 to 10, while laboratory and rater instructions say 0 to 10. The saved PDF does not resolve the administered minimum (PDF pp. 9, 32, 34).

The printed participant-assistance model is ChatGPT-4.2. Its release year is not supplied, so ai_tool.year is null and the model name is not silently corrected. Claude is used to classify prompts during analysis, not as the participant assistance (PDF pp. 7, 12, 27).
No pooled AI and No-AI means, SDs, or outcome standardizer accompany the eligible combined-arm regressions. They remain null; Table 1 reports separate incentive-arm summaries only (PDF pp. 14, 23).

No pair-specific total count, contrast SE, test, confidence interval, or effect size accompanies the same-incentive arm comparisons in Table 1. The printed per-arm counts and SDs are retained without deriving new statistics.

DAT is collected after the experimental stages with AI access removed, but the exact elapsed interval and scoring implementation are not stated. No delayed follow-up is reported (PDF p. 8; PDF p. 14 notes; PDF p. 31).
The separate Stage 2 paper and its exact analyzed sample overlap are not identified (PDF p. 8).

External-file completeness could not be independently checked in this extraction. Anonymous urllib requests with User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1 to https://api.figshare.com/v2/articles/32132980 and the named Mendeley Data file-list API for t93pf5r6fp version 2 both failed with WinError 10013 (socket access forbidden). No external statistics or unverified metadata values were added.
notes: Independent extraction B on 2026-10-10. The complete markdown conversion was read in contiguous chunks covering all 119358 characters, including appendices and references. All main-text tables, both figures, and Appendix C Table 1 were inspected; every cited numeric source was checked using PyMuPDF page text. Table extraction was also attempted with find_tables; the printed text preserves the relevant rows. Statistical inventory: Table 1 prints means, SDs, and analyzed arm counts for average creativity, character count, and DAT; these supply the nine full-arm comparisons. Table 5 columns (1)-(3) print the three full-sample AI coefficients, robust SEs, significance markers, and analyzed counts; pooled means/SDs, contrast CIs, and standardized effects are absent. Table 2 contains post-treatment-adjusted or subgroup creativity associations, Tables 3 and Appendix C Table 1 contain mediation analyses, and Table 4 concerns use/process measures. These excluded analyses are listed in not_extracted. Figures 1 and 2 are a timeline and conceptual mediation diagram, with no outcome statistics to digitize. The external-rater survey is the measurement component of S1, not another independent experiment assigning creative producers to AI. The nine cell comparisons retain every participant in the named assigned arms; they do not stratify by realized AI use. No cross-incentive comparison is invented as an AI-design contrast. Numeric values are transcribed without computing differences, sums, SDs, SEs, standardized effects, or p-values; source quotes preserve printed precision, including trailing zeros. n_units is null because the analysis unit is the participant and no distinct output/rating count is needed.
